title: Real panel lit through a bottom-contact FPC breakout with design.py's J3 map; redraw timed
procedure: before any power, put the FPC into the breakout contacts down (assembly.md section 5 step 6); diode-test to find which header pin is panel 1 (LEDA, forward to 2 and 3) and check continuity among panel 11-24 and 34 (GND); record the breakout header pin each panel pin lands on (it must equal 51 minus the FH12 pad number); then wire an ESP32-S3 dev board by the panel's own pin names on its 8080 8-bit bus (1 LEDA, 2-3 LEDK, 7-8 IM0 and IM1 high, 9 IM2 low, 10 RESET, 25-32 DB7-DB0, 35 RD high, 36 WRX, 37 D/CX, 38 CSX low, 39 TE, 40-42 VDDI/VCI); read ID4 (0xD3) with RD driven for the read only; light each cathode pin (LEDK1, LEDK2: three LEDs each) in turn from the bench supply through 47 ohm; then time a full 320 x 480 redraw in RGB565 at 20 MHz and at 25 MHz (twc 40 ns, ili9488.txt:16159) and a battle-text update
pass_limit: each cathode pin lights at 20 mA and its voltage at 60 mA is recorded; ID4 reads 0x94 0x88; the recorded breakout-to-panel map equals 51 minus the FH12 pad number for every contact; a colour fill shows no missing line at 25 MHz; a full redraw and a text update within REQ-DSP-11's numbers (12.3 ms of bus time at 25 MHz in RGB565, VER-199)
evidence: DROPPED with esp32s3 (tag vv-esp32s3-final): the panel lit from an ESP32-S3 dev board; the chip gate lights it from the F1C200s dev board (VER-224); its last result there was NOT_RUN

title: Panel FPC tail thickness and width against the FH12-50S
procedure: calipers (about $15 if not owned) on the stiffened tail at three points
pass_limit: tail 0.30 +-0.05 mm (the panel's drawing: 0.3 +-0.03) and 25.5 +-0.07 mm wide at the contacts; exposed contact length >= 3 mm

title: Comb pill resistance on ENIG, on a bare board from the order
procedure: a bare board from the same JLC order (same ENIG bath and mask), on day one before any assembled unit is powered; press a DS Lite pill with a 1 N weight on every contact; DMM ohms (a $2 coupon ordered now is advisory only)
pass_limit: < 1 kohm on every contact, 10 presses each

title: Comb leakage at 4.2 V, clean and after humidity
procedure: on the same bare board: 4.2 V from the bench supply through the comb into a DMM on volts (10 Mohm input); read the leakage from the divider
pass_limit: >= 100 Mohm (DMM reads <= 0.38 V) clean, after a damp-cloth wipe and after 24 h in a sealed box with a wet sponge
needs: the 5 bare boards from the JLC order, 14d

title: Latch replica on SOT-23 breakouts (disputed: Fable only)
procedure: build Q1, D2, D3, R13-R15, R42, U3 from the real LCSC parts; drive PWR_HOLD from a Pico 2 through a watchdog reset

title: Printed case with real parts: fit, screws, caps, panel in the top

pass_limit: closes without force; caps 1.85 +-0.2 mm proud and free; panel window aligned within 0.5 mm; nothing rattles; the evidence names the case release hash

title: Cell incoming inspection per lot
procedure: every cell: DMM on the plug (red lead on J2 pin 1 '+'), OCV; the plug latches in a Molex 53261-0271 sample and withdraws only with the latch pressed; one per lot: calipers with its PCM; run before the first cell is plugged (F-R9: the cells take 21 days to arrive)

title: Button force and travel against a genuine DS Lite
procedure: kitchen scale (0.1 g) under the cap, press until the pill closes (DMM continuity); depth gauge or calipers for travel
pass_limit: force within +-30% of the genuine DS Lite measured the same way; travel within +-0.2 mm
needs: a printed case (VER-48) and a genuine DS Lite (owned), 0d

title: Pill-to-comb XY registration measured on the fit kit

pass_limit: every pill print centred within 0.9 mm of its comb centre
needs: a printed fit kit (CASE), 0d

title: BU-0 unpowered resistances to GND (TP1-TP4) and VBUS-VBAT
procedure: the RP2350B board's bring-up doc (to be written), step 0: resistance to GND of VBUS, the cell, each rail and the system rail, unpowered
pass_limit: TP1 8.5-10 kohm (R38 10k in parallel with R14 47k + D3 + R15 100k, about 147 kohm when the meter forward-biases D3, and R43 220k + EN1's internal 285k: 9.19 kohm with D3 on, 9.81 kohm with it off, at 71737ae's values); TP2, TP3 and TP4 > 1 kohm once the caps charge (TP3 above 1 kohm rules out a U2 BAT-to-pad bridge: DF-219); TP1 to TP3 > 10 kohm; none a short

title: BU-0 diode tests VBAT<->VSYS and VBUS<->VSYS
procedure: bring-up step 0: diode tests across the power path (the cell, the system rail, VBUS), unpowered
pass_limit: TP3(+) to TP2: one diode drop, 0.4-0.8 V (U2's battery FET's body diode); TP2(+) to TP3: open or above 1.2 V; TP1(+) to TP2: open (U2's input switch blocks both ways); bringup.md step 0 to match (DEF-21)

title: BU-0 cell polarity at J2 before mating
procedure: bring-up step 0: the cell's polarity at its header with a meter before first mating
pass_limit: red lead on J2 pin 1 '+', checked with a DMM, every cell
needs: cells (AliExpress, 21d)

title: BU-1 USB only, no cell
procedure: hardware/ref_design/docs/bringup.md step 1: first power from the bench supply at 5.0 V with a 100 mA limit through a USB-C breakout, never a wall charger first (DF-101); USB power meter
pass_limit: VBUS 4.75-5.25 V; VSYS 4.30-4.50 V (U2's OUT); 3V3 3.25-3.35 V (the TLV75733P's +-1.5%); input < 120 mA; the ESP32-S3's USB Serial/JTAG enumerates within 5 s; CHG_PG_N low
evidence: DROPPED with esp32s3 (tag vv-esp32s3-final): bring-up step 1 enumerated the ESP32-S3's USB Serial/JTAG; VER-237 boots the RP2350B board; its last result there was NOT_RUN

title: BU: all 20 contacts read, alone and together
procedure: bring-up: each of the 20 contacts read by the bare-metal image, alone and in every pair, seat 1's Start also through the buffered power-key line
pass_limit: each contact reads pressed when shorted and released otherwise, on its own GPIO as the pin file gives; any 4 at once read correctly; CHG_PG_N and CHG_STAT_N follow the charger

title: BU-2.2/2.3 ADC7 and the charger's status pins
procedure: hardware/ref_design/docs/bringup.md steps 2.2-2.3
pass_limit: ADC7 reads; CHG_STAT_N and CHG_PG_N read with the pull-downs off; CHG_PG_N low on USB

procedure: bring-up: 10 full frames of a checker pattern over the 8080 bus at the firmware's write clock, read back and compared

title: BU-3.5 backlight current, balance, step response, headroom
procedure: bring-up: the backlight current at the firmware's lowest and highest duty, its step response, its headroom at the cutoff
pass_limit: 80% duty: 99 +-5 mV on R52 and R53, within 3 mV of each other; at the firmware's highest duty: <= 120 mA total through JP2; at its minimum duty (18%, pinmap.md) each sink within +-25%; 18<->95% step: no ringing on the scope; a 3.5 V cell at the highest duty: drop <= 5%; USB plugged in while lit: no visible flash; with 3V3 off (the device off), the cell and then USB plugged in, and 3V3 switched on with BL_PWM low: under 5 mA through JP2 for under 10 us on the scope (REQ-DSP-09: VER-05 prints these only as estimates); BL_PWM low with 3V3 on: the current through JP2 recorded (VER-05: up to 4.13 mA, DEF-96)

title: BU-3.6 tearing-effect pulse
procedure: bring-up: the panel's TE pulse on the scope with TEON set
pass_limit: one pulse per frame, 60 Hz +-10%

title: BU-4 audio: level, carrier, wake, heat, noise

title: BU-5.1 off-state cell current
procedure: bring-up: the cell current with the device off and no USB, a DMM across the board's off-current jumper
pass_limit: <= 30 uA at 25 C, cell 3.7-4.2 V, device off, no USB (designed: R17 into U10's clamped input about 7.9 uA at a 4.2 V cell since 71737ae, 4.5 uA through the 940k divider before; U2 from BAT, U7 in shutdown on the live VSYS, U3 off; the TPS3421, fed from 3V3, unpowered and drawing 0 uA, with no current into its input from seat 1's Start's line)

title: BU-5.2 charge current and CHG_OFF pause

pass_limit: 242-295 mA into a cell at 3.6-3.9 V (R5 3.3k) and still >= 242 mA after 10 min with U2's top under ambient + 50 C; CHG_OFF high stops it within 1 s; low resumes

title: BU-5.3 ADC against a meter; CV at charge-done; bench-supply sweep
procedure: bring-up: the firmware's cell reading against a meter across the cell's range; the CV at charge-done
pass_limit: computed VBAT within 20 mV of the DMM at 3.50 V after calibration (VER-155) and within 50 mV elsewhere above 3.6 V; VBAT 4.158-4.242 V when CHG_STAT_N goes high at the end of a charge
instrument: handheld DMM, 0.5% + 2 counts; checked against the 4.096 V reference that session
needs: 10 ohm 5 W resistor and a 4.096 V reference breakout (LM4040 or REF3040, about $3, 7d)

title: BU-5.4 charger heat and the TS level
procedure: bring-up: the charger's heat and its thermistor input through a full charge at 25 C
pass_limit: TS within design_numbers.py tsband's band at the ambient read beside the board (about 0.70-1.04 V at 22 C; 0.75 V nominal holds only at 25 C: round 2's objection); after 10 min of charging in the closed case still >= 0.46 V (TH1 under 35 C: B4460 at 75 uA, 6.15 kohm); U2's top under ambient + 50 C

title: BU-5.4a charge pauses outside the temperature window
procedure: bring-up: the charge pauses with the thermistor held hot and held cold
pass_limit: pauses at VER-32's hot edge +-3 C rising (47 C nominal) and its cold edge +-3 C falling (3.5 C nominal); resumes in range

title: BU-5.5 unplug on the scope; 100 unplugs with a flash check
procedure: bring-up: USB unplugged at full load on the scope, each rail in range; then 100 unplugs, the flash read back and its CRC checked after each
pass_limit: VBAT at the trigger 3.50 +-0.03 V; VSYS never below VBAT - 0.10 V; 3V3 >= 3.135 V throughout; 100 unplugs with no reset and no flash CRC error

title: BU-5.6 hot plug with no cell
procedure: bring-up: a live plug-in from a 2 m cable with no cell, VBUS and the system rail on the scope
pass_limit: VBUS at or under U2's OVP minimum less 0.2 V (as VER-12); VSYS <= 4.6 V; EN1 (U2 pin 6) <= 6.7 V; PWR_EN (TP6) <= 5.7 V (as VER-12); bringup.md step 5.6 to match (DEF-21)

title: BU-5.7 U3's EN at a live plug-in
procedure: hardware/ref_design/docs/bringup.md step 5.7 (scope TP6 PWR_EN and TP2, cell in, board off)
pass_limit: PWR_EN <= 5.5 V at every instant (the TLV75733P's EN recommended maximum, tlv757p.txt:208), 10 plug-ins
evidence: DROPPED with esp32s3 (tag vv-esp32s3-final): U3's EN at a live plug-in: the ESP32-S3 board's TLV75733P enable; its last result there was NOT_RUN

title: BU-6 power switch: on, latch, off, reset
procedure: hardware/ref_design/docs/bringup.md step 6 (bringup.md 6.2-6.3 still say Y: DEF-21)
pass_limit: on only after Start held 1.0 +-0.2 s; off after a long press; RESET turns it off on the cell; off current back <= 30 uA
evidence: DROPPED with esp32s3 (tag vv-esp32s3-final): the power switch SW24's latch; VER-240 tests the power slider; its last result there was NOT_RUN

title: First power with the rails cut from the chip (catch a wrong regulator before it reaches it)
procedure: bring-up: first power of unit 1 with the regulators' outputs cut from the RP2350B at a jumper, each rail read before the chip sees it
pass_limit: 3V3_LDO 3.20-3.40 V before JP1 is bridged

title: Chip identity and stepping, logged per unit
procedure: picotool info -a (chip ID, package, stepping, flash JEDEC ID) at first boot; write it to the unit's record
pass_limit: RP2354B, 2 MB flash; stepping recorded (A2 means E9 applies to AMP_EN and BL_PWM)
evidence: RETIRED in 39cc07f: the RP2354B left; the module's identity (chip, flash, PSRAM, MAC) is VER-210's (was: NOT_BUILT at no commit)

title: Production self-test image
procedure: a self-test image for the RP2350B board on the generated pin file: contacts, pin neighbour bridges, panel ID, audio, the flash's ID, the USB device's enumeration, the cell reading
pass_limit: every item PASS on a good unit and FAIL on a seeded fault (a shorted button, a panel unplugged); every 'caught by self-test' pair in bridges.csv is in its pair table; <= 5 min a unit

title: PWR_HOLD release after reset and crash on the real board
procedure: scope PWR_HOLD (IO21, module pin 23; probe D2 pin 2 or R42), TP6 (PWR_EN) and TP4 (+3V3) through a reset on J7's EN pad, a watchdog reset and a panic, on the cell
pass_limit: PWR_HOLD < 0.5 V within 10 ms; 3V3 < 0.5 V within 200 ms of the power key released
evidence: DROPPED with esp32s3 (tag vv-esp32s3-final): PWR_HOLD's release through D2 and IO21; VER-243 tests the RP2350B board's power hold; its last result there was NOT_BUILT

title: Start with 1 kohm in series still turns the device on (both Start domes)
procedure: 1 kohm in series with each Start dome in turn (SW21, then SW23: across its pads in place of a press); bench supply as the cell at 3.50 V
pass_limit: for each dome: 3V3 >= 3.20 V within 50 ms; PWR_BTN_N (SW21) or P2_START (SW23) reads low; Q1's or Q7's gate margin over its maximum Vgs(th) (q1.json) reported in volts
evidence: RETIRED in 39cc07f: the Starts left the power path (Q7, D8, R62 gone); the power button SW24 is VER-211's (was: NOT_BUILT at no commit)

title: Start leakage immunity and per-unit dome leakage (both Start domes)
procedure: 1 Mohm across SW21's pads, then across SW23's, cell at 4.2 V, no USB; then each unit's leakage from the VSYS ring to the centre pad of both domes as VER-46
pass_limit: the device stays off (3V3 < 0.5 V) for 10 min with either; every unit's SW21 and SW23 >= 100 Mohm
evidence: RETIRED in 39cc07f: as VER-78: SW24's leakage immunity is VER-211's (was: NOT_BUILT at no commit)

title: USB sources, cables and orientations
procedure: both plug orientations on a USB-C charger, a PC port, a USB-A to C cable and an Android phone (the host), each enumerating as the console's WebUSB device
pass_limit: charges and enumerates in both orientations on every source; no limit cycling at 500 mA; the console never sources VBUS; every cable seats fully, case closed
needs: USB-C breakout (about $5, 5d) and a PD charger (owned?)

title: Input current from a default-power USB port
procedure: a USB power meter between a PC's USB-A port and the console, charging and playing
pass_limit: input current <= 500 mA within 2 s of plug-in from a default-power port (U2's USB500 limit, 475 mA), the backlight at full and a flat cell charging

title: Charge path after charge-done plus 1 h (unit 1 confirmation)
procedure: unit 1, after charge-done plus 1 h: the cell's current and voltage
pass_limit: VBAT <= 4.242 V after 1 h at charge-done; the cell current 0 to -5 mA (U2 off the cell until VBAT falls 100 mV, then a top-up)

title: 3V3 regulation and 3V3 load
procedure: a bench supply into VBUS and one in place of the cell: each rail's voltage at no load and at full load
pass_limit: 3V3 3.20-3.40 V at every point; 3V3 load <= 150 mA

title: 1V1 core rail level and ripple
procedure: scope on TP9 (1V1), 20 MHz limit, ground spring, at idle and at full CPU load
pass_limit: within the RP2350's DVDD range (Table 1688: write the values into this row on first use) including ripple
evidence: RETIRED in 39cc07f: the 1V1 core rail left with the RP2354B (was: NOT_BUILT at no commit)

title: Cell surface temperature over a full charge in the closed case
procedure: attended, in a LiPo bag on a tile (VER-172); K-type thermocouple taped to the cell (a DMM with a thermocouple input, about $25 if not owned); log every minute; 25 C room, then a 35 C box
pass_limit: <= 45 C at 25 C ambient; <= the cell maker's charge maximum at 35 C
needs: DMM with thermocouple input (about $25, 2d)

title: Touch temperature during charge-while-playing
procedure: the firmware rule from VER-144 in the image first; thermocouples on the face over U2, the back over U7 and the hottest spot found by touch; 1 h charge-while-playing, backlight 100%, audio full scale
pass_limit: <= 43 C (target) at 25 C ambient; measured rise + the rated maximum ambient <= 48 C (IEC 62368-1 TS1 limit for plastic held 10 min to 8 h)

title: The thermistor tracks the cell during charge
procedure: two thermocouples: one at the cell's centre and one on its end facing TH1; TH1 from the TS voltage (VER-68); one full charge in the closed case
pass_limit: TH1 within 5 C of the cell's hotter point throughout
needs: a second thermocouple (about $3, 7d)

title: Cell protection (PCM) trip test on a spare pack
procedure: bench supply into the pack: raise to find OVP, discharge through a resistor to find UVP, short through 0.1 ohm for OCP
pass_limit: OVP 4.25-4.35 V; UVP 2.4-3.0 V; OCP trips (or the spec sheet's values) on one pack per lot

title: Assembled-board inspection under the microscope (IPC-A-610 Class 2)
procedure: the RP2350B board's assembly doc (to be written): every assembled board under the microscope to IPC-A-610 Class 2
pass_limit: no bridge, tombstone, lifted lead or missing part; every pin 1 as the silk; every unit
subsystems: power cell soc display audio buttons usbc storage

title: Board flatness on arrival
procedure: board on a glass plate, feeler gauges (about $5) at the corners
pass_limit: bow and twist <= 0.75% of the board's length: 1.14 mm over 151.48 mm (the Edge.Cuts outline at 71737ae, y 24.26 to 175.74; case.scad's board_l)

title: Hand assembly demo and time study
procedure: the RP2350B board's assembly doc: Alex assembles one unit, timed, in the doc's safe order (no work next to a plugged cell)
pass_limit: one unit in <= 30 min with a screwdriver and a knife; no part damaged; no connector mated or unmated with the tub lifting the cell's leads; the cell plug never offered to J4; cell and panel each swap in <= 10 min
needs: ESD mat and strap (about $15, 2d)

title: Case open/close cycling
procedure: 20 open/close cycles with the six screws at the length VER-147 sets, as assembly.md step 8; the case closed with the cell unplugged; after the cycles: C53 (the MLCC nearest a boss) at 40x and TP4 to GND re-measured
pass_limit: no cracked key or grip rib and no stripped boss; the top still seats; C53 (the MLCC nearest a boss, 11.4 mm from H5) uncracked and TP4 > 1 kohm; the evidence names the case release hash

title: Drop test
procedure: unit 4 (sacrificial, gates.md allocation): 3 drops from 1.0 m onto hardwood on the face, an end and a corner (IEC 62368-1 Annex T.7, to confirm); re-run on the DVT spin when a change record asks
pass_limit: still works; no crack that exposes the cell or a board; cell moved <= 1 mm; plug and FPC still seated

title: Button life cycling
procedure: unit 4 or a bare board in a printed case: a hobby servo and a Pico press one button of each type (about $10 of parts)
pass_limit: 100,000 presses with contact resistance staying < 1 kohm
needs: hobby servo and a Pico (about $10, 7d)

title: First board: the program runs in place from a 16 MB flash on the RP2350B
procedure: on an RP2350B with a 16 MB QSPI flash wired as Raspberry Pi's minimal design draws it (the first assembled board, at EVT; moved from the chip gate on 2026-10-30): the bare-metal battler linked to the flash's addresses with code and a block of sound data (sequences, instruments and compressed samples) placed in the flash's upper half, power-cycled 20 times; at each start it runs in place (XIP), reads the flash's JEDEC ID, reads all 16 MB through the XIP window and compares its CRC with the image's, and runs the sound mixer for 10 min at 8 channels and 32 kHz, reading its sequences, instruments and compressed samples from the flash in place, while the display redraws at full rate. Firmware consequence (rp2350.pdf Release 8, pdftotext -layout lines 799, 21999 and 22549): 16 MB is the chip's documented size for its first flash slot (line 799, 'Up to 16 MB of external QSPI flash or PSRAM through dedicated QSPI bus'); bootable partitions must lie wholly in the first 16 MB flash window (line 21999, 'Bootable partitions must reside wholly in the first 16 MB flash window'); and the boot ROM maps only the booted partition, 'with a maximum size of 16 MB', and an access beyond it bus-faults (line 22549, 'maximum size of 16 MB'), so a partition's address translation spans only that partition and the sound data outside the booted partition must be mapped by the firmware itself (QMI ATRANS), which this check's CRC read of all 16 MB and its mixer run exercise
pass_limit: 20 of 20 power-ons run in place from the flash to the lobby; the JEDEC ID is the GD25Q128's (0xC84018: to confirm); the 16 MB CRC matches; the mixer runs 8 channels at 32 kHz for 10 min with 0 underruns (REQ-SOC-01, REQ-SOC-02, REQ-PRD-18, REQ-PRD-08.B)
needs: the first assembled board (no separate dev board); an SWD probe or a USB-UART lead (owned, 0d)

title: The flash's wiring against Raspberry Pi's RP2350B minimal design (circuit_checks.py flashwiring)
procedure: to write: circuit_checks.py flashwiring reads design.py and the minimal design's net list (hardware/ref_design/datasheets once VER-233 has put it there) and compares, net for net: QSPI SCLK, QSPI SS and QSPI SD0 to QSPI SD3 each from the flash's pin to the RP2350B's QSPI pin of the same name and on no other net; the flash's VCC on the IO rail with the decoupling capacitor the drawing gives; the QSPI SS pull-up and its BOOTSEL pad; the flash's package pin order; --seed swaps QSPI SD1 and QSPI SD2 and must fail
pass_limit: RESULT: PASS: 0 differences from the minimal design in the flash's nets, passives and pull-ups (REQ-SOC-09)
needs: the minimal design's schematic or net list on disk (VER-233, 1d)

title: The chip's and the flash's footprints against the minimal design and the makers' drawings

pass_limit: RESULT: PASS: 0 unexplained differences in pad count, pitch, pin 1 and exposed pad for both parts, and no QSPI track more than 2 mm longer than the minimal design's longest (REQ-SOC-09)
needs: the GD25Q128's package drawing on disk (VER-233, 1d)

title: Sound engine on a unit: 8 channels at 32 kHz, 30 min of battling with no dropout
procedure: unit 1 on its cell: the battler plays its music from note sequences on sampled instruments and the 4 synthesized channels (two squares, wave, noise) and its cries and effects from compressed samples, all read in place from the flash, through 30 min of battling at the full display rate and 50% backlight; the mixer's channel count and sample rate read from the firmware, the audio buffer's underrun counter logged, the chosen source (PWM or I2S) and the amplifier at -12 dBFS

title: The 16 MB flash's budget and read bandwidth on paper

title: The hard reset on paper: the TPS3421 on seat 1's Start's line, its delay and the RUN pin
procedure: from tps3421.pdf (TI SBVS211B, LCSC C2067262 = TPS3421EGDRYR) and rp2350.pdf (Release 8), with the register's described circuit (no schematic exists yet): the TPS3421 variants and TS pin, and which gives the nearest delay to 8 s, with its minimum and maximum over temperature and supply, against the 2.5 s turn-on hold; its inputs (PB1 and PB2, levels, pull-up) against Start's 3V3-side buffered line; its output (type, pulse width, re-arming) against the RP2350's RUN pin; its supply range and current from 3V3; what the diode-OR power path does when the hold fires with Start held; the RP2350 reset-reason register (CHIP_RESET) and what it separates; the watchdog's maximum and resolution and what its reset does to PWR_HOLD; RP2350-E9 against R42; REQ-PWR-10's arithmetic. The circuit-dependent items (no voltage on the unpowered part's pins in any power state, Start turning the unit on with it unpowered) stay with VER-159 and VER-239 at the schematic. Written up in analysis/power_off_datasheet_check_2026-10-30.md
pass_limit: RESULT: PASS: a variant and delay-select setting exist whose delay is about 8 s, with its delay over temperature and supply inside 6 s to 10 s (Alex, 2026-10-29: REQ-SOC-04), so its minimum is also above the 2.5 s turn-on hold (the turn-on hold never resets the unit); its output drives RUN low and releases it (open-drain against RUN's pull-up), and what it does after the delay is recorded; its supply range includes 3V3 and its quiescent current is inside the 3V3 budget; the datasheets show how a held Start behaves after the reset and a reset-reason register separates a RUN-pin reset from a power-on and a watchdog reset; the watchdog's maximum is at least 2 s; R42 meets RP2350-E9's 8.2 kohm limit (REQ-SOC-04, REQ-PRD-08.B, REQ-PWR-09, REQ-PWR-10)
evidence: hardware/vv/evidence/2026-10-30_VER-258_power_off_datasheets.txt

title: The boot ROM's recovery on paper and on the stripboard: partition table, A/B slots, hash check, UF2 over a valid table, block protection
procedure: from the RP2350 datasheet's boot sequence, partition table, hash check, try-before-you-buy (flash update boot) and USB boot mode chapters, and the GD25Q128 datasheet's block protection (BP bits, SRP, WP#, volatile or not), answer in writing with a datasheet line each: (1) how a dragged firmware .uf2 picks slot A or B; (2) whether the boot ROM accepts a whole-flash (absolute) UF2 over a valid partition table, else the recovery step is `picotool erase` and then the one file; (3) that a blank flash, a corrupted image and a corrupted partition table each drop to USB boot mode by themselves; (4) that a failed update falls back to the previous firmware; (5) whether a recovery .uf2 can rewrite a bootloader locked by block protection (DF-263); (6) the BOOTSEL pad on QSPI SS; (7) the UF2 drive's driverless enumeration on Windows, macOS and Linux; then settle (1), (2), (3) and (5) with a try on the stripboard Pico 2 (an RP2350A: the same boot ROM) and a flash with block protection
pass_limit: RESULT: PASS: all 7 answered with a datasheet line or a recorded try, each answer that differs from the assumption in REQ-PRD-08.B, REQ-PRD-19 or REQ-SOC-10 logged as a defect or a decision for Alex before the order (REQ-PRD-19, REQ-SOC-10, REQ-PRD-08.B)
needs: the RP2350 and GD25Q128 datasheets on disk (VER-233, 1d); the stripboard Pico 2 and picotool (owned, 0d)

title: Update by dragging a .uf2 to the unit's USB drive on Windows, macOS and Linux: the recovery file and the firmware file
procedure: unit 1 in its case, on Windows, on macOS and on Linux, 3 tries each: put the unit in update mode (seat 1's Select at power-on) and note that its drive appears with no driver to install; (a) recovery: from an erased flash, from a corrupted image and from a corrupted partition table, copy the one recovery .uf2 and time it from the copy to the lobby; read back the partition table, bootloader, firmware and sound hashes; (b) firmware: copy a firmware .uf2 alone and time it; read back that the bootloader and the sound hashes are unchanged; and if VER-259 finds the boot ROM refuses a whole-flash UF2 over a valid table, do (a) as `picotool erase` and then the one file
pass_limit: 3 of 3 tries each way on each of the three systems; no driver or administrator prompt; the recovery file restores a unit in 3 min or less with the partition table, bootloader, firmware and sound all matching; the firmware file installs in 30 s or less and leaves the rest untouched (REQ-PRD-19)
needs: a Windows, a macOS and a Linux computer (Alex has some: to confirm); picotool (0d)

title: The pin budget at the architecture stage: 48 GPIOs against every function, with the relief option named
procedure: before the pin plan (VER-232), count the GPIOs each function takes from the RP2350B's 48 (GPIO0 to 47; QSPI and USB are dedicated pins and not counted): the 8-bit 8080 panel bus (eight data lines, WR, RD, D/C and CS: 12) with TE and RST (14), the backlight PWM (1), the audio output (1) and the amplifier enable (1), the power hold (1), the charger's status (PG, STAT: 2) and its CE (1), the cell sense on an ADC pin (1), the debug UART (TX and RX: 2) and the 20 inputs read directly (the 20 contacts: 20; seat 1's Start is also the power key, read through its buffered line, so it takes no pin of its own). Claude's count is 44 of 48, 4 spare (5 with RD tied high). If the count is over, the 74HC165 chain (about $0.95 a unit at 10, 3 pins for 20 inputs, freeing about 18) is the designated pin-relief option and the first thing to change (Alex, 2026-10-29)
pass_limit: RESULT: PASS: the count is 46 or fewer of the 48 GPIOs (2 spare or more, Claude's margin), every ADC-capable and strap pin use is listed, and the relief option's cost and the pins it frees are stated; over that, the relief option is applied in the pin plan before the schematic (REQ-SOC-05)

title: Sleep and resume on unit 1: the saved battle, the 1 s off, the build-ID discard
procedure: unit 1 in a local battle with known HP, status, boosts and field: choose Sleep from the pause menu 10 times, timing the screen to the rails below 0.5 V on a scope; power on with Start held 2.5 s each time and compare every Pokemon's state and both players' choice screens against the state before Sleep; then once with the cell unplugged between; in an online battle (the phone bridge) check that Sleep is not offered; flash firmware with another build ID over a saved battle and power on, 3 times, and with one bit of the save flipped, 3 times
pass_limit: off within 1 s of choosing Sleep and back at the same battle with every Pokemon's state identical, 10 of 10, including after the cell was unplugged; no Sleep in an online battle; a save from another build, or one that fails its check, starts at the lobby 3 of 3 (REQ-PRD-20, REQ-SOC-11)
needs: a second firmware build (0d); the phone bridge (VER-251)

title: The Sleep save on paper: its size, its region, its write time and a power cut during the write
procedure: from the battle state's size in the core crates (every Pokemon's HP, status, boosts and the field, both parties) and the GD25Q128 datasheet's sector erase and page program times and its erase endurance: the snapshot's size against the 16 KB limit, the erase plus program time against the 1 s from choosing Sleep to power off, the rotation over sectors and the writes it allows over the unit's life against the endurance and the debug log's use of the same region (DF-259), and the all-or-nothing write (a valid-marker written last, the build ID and the check value read at power-on): a cut at every step leaves the old save or none
pass_limit: RESULT: PASS: the snapshot is 16 KB or less; the write is under 0.5 s (half the 1 s of REQ-PRD-20); the rotation holds 10000 Sleeps under the flash's endurance; a power cut at any step of the write leaves the previous valid save or no valid save (REQ-SOC-11)

title: Flat-shelf recharge test
procedure: 3 units run down to the firmware cutoff on battle play, switched off, left off with no USB for 2 months at 25 C; then each plugged into a 5 V USB source of 0.5 A or more on the charging screen
pass_limit: 3 of 3 units reach charge-done (CHG_STAT_N high with CHG_PG_N low) within REQ-PRD-04.B's 4.0 h plus 1 h, and each then plays REQ-PRD-03.B's battle run for 1 h or more; no cell swollen (thickness within the cell datasheet's maximum)
